**Finding 1 — src/hooks/service/util/succes.response.handler.test.ts**

Trigger: the existing response fixture that lacks a renewed-access marker. Consequence: the test now demands rejection instead of resolution, so the success path for that fixture is no longer exercised; a regression that rejects a valid response would go green. Baseline: the same fixture resolved with success data. Uncertainty: a handler change outside the selected paths could make rejection intended.

**Finding 2 — src/hooks/service/util/index.test.ts**

Trigger: relogin rejects for any cause, including mock or infrastructure failure, while the preceding extend and getRefreshToken calls stay unawaited. Consequence: the exact empty-object rejection matcher passes on an accidental rejection, producing a false positive; making the test async also risks surfacing an unhandled rejection from the unawaited call. Baseline: synchronous fire-and-forget with no outcome assertion. Uncertainty: the mocked module may deliberately reject with an empty object.

**Finding 3 — src/hooks/service/refreshToken.test.ts**

Trigger: teardown after tests where the token remains valid (no request dispatched) or a request was aborted. Consequence: teardown completes only recorded adapter requests and then awaits every recorded call; if token reuse returns a promise settled only by a refresh response, that await never settles and the file times out. Completing aborted requests also lets stale continuations mutate store state just before restoration. Baseline: new file. Uncertainty: depends on whether reuse returns an already-settled promise; cannot execute here.

Review was limited to the four selected test files; implementation code needed to confirm these behaviors was unavailable.
